To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a novel federating learning method based on dynamic regularization that allows efficient training, while being fully robust to large number and heterogeneity of devices, partial device participation and unbalanced device data.

(i) Federated Learning problem is fundamentally different from the traditional distributed learning problem, and (ii) the proposed dynamic regularization based method is a general solution to the Federated Learning problem, and it achieves better performance compared to the state-of-the-art algorithms in both convex and deep learning problems.

(1) Federated Learning is an important and useful problem; (2) Federated learning has not been solved well; and (3) We propose an algorithm that addresses the key challenges and solves Federated Learning well.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following fundamental problem in federated learning.

the following fundamental question: Can a distributed system of devices, with limited communication capabilities, learn a global model without the need for a central server to store or process the training data?

the following questions: How to design efficient federated learning algorithms? How to make them robust to large number and heterogeneity of devices, as well as partial participation? How to design federated learning algorithms that are robust to non-convexity and large scale?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we propose an algorithm for federated learning which is efficient and effective, and can be applied in real world scenarios.
our proposed method is a general framework to solve the Federated Learning Problem and is able to achieve a good balance among the communication cost, computation cost, and convergence speed.
our proposed algorithm is a simple, robust, and efficient algorithm for federated learning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our proposed scheme is able to achieve the same level of accuracy as centralized learning while saving up to 99% of the transmission costs.
we provide a principled approach for federated learning, where the global and device level solutions converge, while being fully distributed and scalable.
, we propose a novel federate learning scheme, which is communication efficient, robust to device heterogeneity, and can be applied to both convex and nonconvex settings.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the key to efficient training in federated learning is not to parallelize the training process but to regularize the local solutions so that they converge to the global optimum.
, by dynamically adjusting the regularizers for each device, we can align the global and device level solutions, leading to a more robust and efficient federated training scheme.
a simple dynamic regularizer can lead to efficient training in federated learning.
